# Instruments: Drum kits

A note's `pitch` uses the **GM drum key**. Latest list: `muser instruments --family drums`.

| instrument | Recommended range | Polyphony | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `drums.808` | 35–81 | 24 | TR-808 style: long-tail low kick, crisp clap; hip-hop / trap / electronic |
| `drums.909` | 35–81 | 24 | TR-909 style: punchy kick and cymbals; house / techno |
| `drums.606` | 35–81 | 24 | TR-606 style: light and crisp; acid / electro |
| `drums.cr78` | 35–81 | 24 | CR-78 style: soft and vintage, with shaker, cowbell and bongos |
| `drums.acoustic` | 35–81 | 24 | Acoustic drum kit (physical modeling); pop / rock / jazz |
| `drums.trap` | 35–81 | 24 | trap kit: heavy kick, crisp snare and clap; suited to rapid closed-hat rolls |
| `drums.techno` | 35–81 | 24 | techno kit: kick with a rumbling tail, hard clap |
| `drums.house` | 35–81 | 24 | house kit: four-on-the-floor kick, clap, shaker, congas |
| `drums.dnb` | 35–81 | 24 | drum & bass kit: tight snare and deep kick |
| `drums.lofi` | 35–81 | 24 | lo-fi kit: soft, dark, with a 12-bit sampled texture |

## Adjustable parameters (instrument_params)

Override the sound of the chosen instrument/preset; write only the items you want to change, the rest stay as they are. `muser instruments <name>` shows the preset's current values.

Set per drum piece: { "kick": { "tune": -2, "decay": 1.5 }, "38": { "snap": 0.8 } }. Keys can be a GM drum key number or an alias (kick snare clap closed_hat open_hat crash ride tom_low tom_mid tom_high ...).

Each drum piece is adjustable (when automating, write `piece.parameter`, such as `kick.tune`; it takes effect from the next hit):

| Parameter | Range | Automation | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tune` | -24 – 24 st | next note | Drum piece tuning (semitones). Kick -3 is deeper; snare +2 is tighter |
| `decay` | 0.1 – 10 x | next note | Tail length (multiple of the original). 0.5 short; 2 longer (808 long-tail kick) |
| `level` | 0 – 4 x | next note | Volume (multiplier), 1 = unchanged |
| `tone` | 0 – 1 | next note | Tone (varies by drum piece, usually brightness) |
| `snap` | 0 – 1 | next note | Attack snap (varies by drum piece; snare wires for a snare) |
| `texture` | 0 – 1 | next note | Texture (varies by drum piece) |
| `pan` | -1 – 1 | next note | Pan: -1 left to 1 right |

### Tuning examples

- Deeper, longer kick, crisper snare, quiet closed hi-hat

  ```json
  { "instrument": "drums.808", "instrument_params": {"kick": {"tune": -3, "decay": 1.8}, "snare": {"snap": 0.8}, "closed_hat": {"level": 0.6}} }
  ```

## Kits from the yinse library (`yinse:kit/<owner>/<name>`)

Kits measured from recordings live in the [muser-yinse](https://github.com/claw-works/muser-yinse) library, not in muser itself:
install one with `muser yinse install kit/<owner>/<name>` (or put a clone of the library on `MUSER_YINSE_PATH`), then write
`"instrument": "yinse:kit/<owner>/<name>"`. `muser yinse search kit` lists them; `muser instruments yinse:kit/<owner>/<name>` prints the pieces and keys.

| instrument | what |
|---|---|
| `yinse:kit/cloudbeer/acoustic-drums` | Acoustic drum kit fitted by hand to sampled kits: punchy kick, snare with wires, rimshot, side stick, clap, six toms, hi-hats, crash, splash, sizzle crash, ride and bell, flat ride, tambourine, cowbell, vibraslap (GM keys). It was the built-in `yinse.strike.drums` up to 0.6.0 |
| `yinse:kit/virtuosity/drums` | Contemporary jazz kit (Virtuosity Drums, CC0), extracted automatically: kick, several snare strokes, two toms, hi-hats, crash, ride, flat ride, GM percussion |
| `yinse:kit/cloudbeer/jingju-luogu` | Peking-opera percussion 京剧锣鼓 (below). It was the built-in `yinse.strike.luogu` up to 0.6.0 |

- Every piece takes `tune`, `decay`, `level`, `tone`, `pan`, by name or key: `{ "kick": { "tune": -2 }, "49": { "decay": 0.6 } }`;
  automate as `piece.param`. A kit can hand the keys it does not have to a built-in kit (`muser instruments` says which).
- These kits are level-calibrated like built-in instruments (the calibration is in the kit file).
- A project written for 0.6.0 with `yinse.strike.luogu` / `yinse.strike.drums`: `muser migrate --from 0.6.0 --write` renames them.
- Make a kit from your own single hits or an SFZ drum library: `muser yinse extract --kit` (see [yinse-extract.md](yinse-extract.md)).

### Peking-opera percussion: `yinse:kit/cloudbeer/jingju-luogu` (京剧锣鼓)

muser's own kit for Beijing opera, folk wind-and-percussion bands (吹打) and festivals. Every piece is modeled from its vibration modes:
drum heads, gong plates, cymbals and wood each have their own overtone ratios; the big gong falls in pitch after the strike (the "kuang～"),
the small gong rises ("taing"). Write the pieces by name in a `grid` or by key in `notes`:

| pitch | name | piece | sound |
|---|---|---|---|
| 36 | `dagu` | 大鼓 big drum | thick, punchy "dong" (84 Hz with a sub under it and the stick's slap on top), rings over a second |
| 37 | `gubian` | 鼓边 rim of the tanggu | dry click |
| 38 | `tanggu` | 堂鼓 tanggu (the opera's big drum) | a 174 Hz boom with a longer 226 Hz ring, measured from a solo passage |
| 39 | `ban` | 拍板 clapper | hard wooden slap that keeps the beat (板) |
| 40 | `bangu` | 板鼓 bangu | a very high, dry crack around 1.7-1.9 kHz, gone in tens of milliseconds: the conductor of the band |
| 49 | `daluo` | 大锣 big gong | "kuang": a hard stroke starts near 270 Hz and keeps sinking for most of a second (to about 215 Hz, as measured in an opera recording), hardly fading meanwhile, with a strong partial three times higher and a wash of brass above; a soft stroke barely slides |
| 51 | `chaoluo` | 大抄锣 big flat gong (tam-tam kind) | no pitch slide: a low hum around 209 Hz, and a sheet of brass that blooms over the first half second and takes four or five seconds to fade; openings, folk luogu, lion dance |
| 52 | `xiaoluo` | 小锣 small gong | "tai": bright and clear, slides up to 684 Hz (from about 560 Hz when hit hard, less when soft), ringing three seconds |
| 55 | `xiaobo` | 小钹 small cymbals | thin and bright: a bell cluster near 800 Hz under a flat sheet from 2.5 kHz up, a second long |
| 56 | `zhongbo` | 中钹 medium cymbals | between the two: a sheet from 1.3 kHz up, rings three seconds |
| 57 | `naobo` | 大钹 cymbals (nao/bo) | open clash, a dense unpitched sheet of brass strongest at 1-5 kHz, the low part ringing longest; a later 58 chokes it |
| 58 | `naobo_mute` | 大钹闷击 cymbals pressed together | short muted "qi" |
| 75 | `bangzi` | 梆子 bangzi | very high wood, the beat of 梆子腔 operas |
| 76 / 77 | `muyu` / `muyu_low` | 木鱼 wood blocks | high / low |
| 81 | `pengling` | 碰铃 bells | two little bells, beating against each other |

Luogu syllables (锣鼓经) map onto pieces: **仓** (cang) = big gong + cymbals + bangu together; **才** (cai) = cymbals; **台** (tai) = small gong;
**七** (qi) = muted cymbals (58); **大** (da) = one bangu stroke; **嘟** (du) = a bangu roll (strokes getting faster); **令** (ling) = a light small-gong stroke.

- 四击头 (the four-stroke cadence that ends an entrance): 大 大 | 仓 . 才 . | 七 才 | 仓 — —
- 急急风 (fast running): 仓才 仓才 … on every half beat, bangu on every stroke, ending on 仓 七 七 仓.
- 吹打: 大鼓 on the strong beats, 堂鼓 between, 鼓边 on the off-beats, 小钹 on every half beat.
- The pieces of one stroke are written at the same `start`. 仓 stacks three loud pieces: leave headroom (track `gain_db` about -8).
- Per piece: `{ "daluo": { "tune": -3, "decay": 1.5 }, "xiaoluo": { "tune": 2 } }`: a lower, longer big gong for 京剧 "大锣"; `tone` softens or hardens the strike.

## Common rhythm skeletons (4/4, one bar = 4 beats)

- Basic pop/rock: kick on 0, 2; snare on 1, 3; closed hi-hat every 0.5 beat.
- house/techno four-on-the-floor: kick on 0, 1, 2, 3; clap on 1, 3; open hi-hat at 0.5, 1.5, 2.5, 3.5.
- trap (half-time feel): kick on 0, 1.75, 2.5; snare/clap on 2; closed hi-hat every 0.25 beat, with rolls of 0.125 beat in places.
- drum & bass: kick on 0, 2.5; snare on 1, 3; closed hi-hat every 0.5 beat.

## Tips and common mistakes

- A note's `pitch` is a **GM drum key**, not a scale pitch. Using 60 (middle C) triggers the high bongo (cr78 / acoustic) or makes no sound.
- For drum notes a `length` of 0.1-0.25 is enough; the ring-out of crash and open hi-hat is decided by the drum piece itself.
- An open hi-hat (46) followed right away by a closed hi-hat (42) or pedal hi-hat (44) chokes the open hi-hat; this is normal drum-machine behavior.
- Use velocity `velocity` for dynamics: strong beats 0.9-1.0, weak beats 0.6-0.8, ghost notes 0.3-0.4.
